name: Enclomiphene

lead: Enclomiphene is one of the two geometric isomers that make up clomiphene citrate, a drug long prescribed for female ovulatory dysfunction. It was developed as an oral treatment for men whose low testosterone stems from reduced pituitary signalling (secondary hypogonadism).

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is discussed as a way to raise testosterone without injecting it, as a component of post-cycle protocols, and, in some threads, in relation to height or bone growth. Clinical trials exist for the hypogonadism use; none have tested it for appearance outcomes.

paras: Enclomiphene blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus and pituitary. Reduced estrogen feedback is reported to raise luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which prompts the testes to make more testosterone themselves.

Published trials describe short-term safety comparable to placebo and testosterone gel, but long-term data are limited. Forum users report fatigue, mood effects and other complaints. Enclomiphene has no FDA approval, and products obtained outside prescriptions are of uncertain quality. Trial data in teenagers are absent.

lead: Enclomiphene (also called trans-clomiphene; the citrate salt was developed under the name Androxal) is a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator that behaves mainly as an estrogen receptor antagonist. It is the trans-stereoisomer of clomiphene citrate, a drug widely prescribed for decades for ovulatory dysfunction in women [1][2].

Its main investigated use is in men with secondary hypogonadism, where it is reported to raise endogenous testosterone by increasing gonadotropins, while preserving sperm counts in trials that compared it with topical testosterone [1][2][3]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials of clomiphene or enclomiphene reported higher total testosterone, LH and FSH than placebo, with considerable heterogeneity between studies [4].

In online appearance and physique communities, enclomiphene is discussed as a testosterone-raising option, as part of post-cycle or TRT-adjacent protocols, and by some posters in connection with height or bone growth. No published trial has tested it for those purposes, and it is not approved by regulators as a finished drug product.

paras: Clomiphene citrate is a mixture of two geometric isomers: enclomiphene (trans) and zuclomiphene (cis). Enclomiphene acts mostly as an estrogen receptor antagonist, while zuclomiphene has been described as predominantly estrogenic in early rodent work comparing the isomers. Because of this difference, enclomiphene was proposed as a purer way to raise testosterone in men than the racemic mixture [1].

Clomiphene has been used off-label for many years in male hypogonadism, particularly where fertility is a concern [2]. Enclomiphene was developed to provide the antagonist activity without the zuclomiphene component, which pharmacokinetic studies in women found accumulates because it is cleared more slowly [5].

By blocking estrogen receptors at the hypothalamic-pituitary level, enclomiphene reduces negative feedback and is reported to increase LH and FSH release. The testes respond with increased testosterone production, an approach described as restoration of the body's own signalling rather than replacement with exogenous testosterone [1][6].

A pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics study in men with secondary hypogonadism described the relationship between enclomiphene dosing and the testosterone, LH and FSH response [3]. Studies in women receiving clomiphene have measured serum concentrations of the two isomers across treatment cycles [5].

A phase II randomized trial compared oral enclomiphene with 1% topical testosterone gel in men with secondary hypogonadism. Enclomiphene raised morning testosterone, estradiol and LH, and the authors reported that it avoided the fall in sperm concentration seen with topical testosterone [3]. A related report in the Journal of Sexual Medicine compared oral enclomiphene with testosterone gel.

Phase III registrations include a morning-testosterone normalization study in overweight men with secondary hypogonadism (n=181), a safety study (n=499), an extension study (n=300) and a bone mineral density study (n=300) [7][8][9][10]. A BJU International report described a phase III randomized trial in obese hypogonadal men in which enclomiphene raised testosterone and preserved sperm counts, unlike topical testosterone [6]. A phase II trial registered in 2016 examined body composition and metabolic parameters with diet and exercise in men with acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and obesity [11].

A 2023 meta-analysis of men with obesity-related functional androgen deficiency, pooling seven studies of clomiphene or enclomiphene over 1.5 to 4 months, reported significant testosterone increases [12]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials reported a mean difference of about 274 ng/dL in total testosterone versus placebo, no significant difference from testosterone gel, and high heterogeneity across trials [4]. Reviews describe short-term safety as comparable to placebo and gel, and note a favourable effect on fasting glucose in early trials [1][13].

A registered trial of enclomiphene in male infertility was withdrawn [14]. No published trial has examined enclomiphene for height, bone length, facial appearance or physique outcomes in healthy or adolescent males.

Reviews of the clinical trials describe short-term safety as satisfactory and similar to placebo and testosterone gel, while noting that data on long-term use are limited [1][2][13]. Because the compound raises estradiol along with testosterone, trials have measured estradiol and some users on forums attribute symptoms to estrogen changes [3].

Forum posts describe individual reports including fatigue and sleepiness after dosing, numbness or other genital sensations, and changes in mood [15]. These are anecdotal reports and have not been verified in controlled studies.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and physique communities
paras: On looksmax.org, enclomiphene is discussed under headings such as testosterone maxxing, usage by teenagers, and bone or height maxxing [16][17][18][19]. Posters frequently describe it as a way to raise testosterone without testicular shutdown, and ask whether it affects growth plates or how to manage estrogen. Replies in those threads commonly note that testosterone-related pathways are not the main driver of bone length and that growth plates in older teens are mostly closed [16][17].

On T Nation and similar forums, enclomiphene appears in discussions of TRT adjuncts, 'testosterone augmentation therapy', post-cycle therapy and stacks with other compounds [20][21][22][23]. Users describe obtaining it through telehealth clinics and from overseas suppliers; the quality of non-prescription products has not been assessed in the published literature.

Reviews list enclomiphene alongside selective androgen receptor modulators and novel testosterone formulations as an investigational approach to hypogonadism that may preserve fertility [24][25]. Clomiphene isomers have also been examined in unrelated laboratory contexts, such as antiviral activity in cell models [26], and in anti-doping studies of clomiphene metabolism [27].

lore.intro: Forum discussions treat enclomiphene as a testosterone-raising tool, sometimes framed around puberty, height or post-cycle recovery [18][17].

Enclomiphene can help height or bone growth.
It is a safer alternative to testosterone because it preserves fertility and testicle size.
Enclomiphene is useful in post-cycle therapy or after stopping TRT.
Enclomiphene causes fatigue or estrogen spikes in some people.

timeline.event: Rodent studies compare the estrogenic and antiestrogenic activity of enclomiphene and zuclomiphene.
A phase III registration of Androxal in men with secondary hypogonadism begins [28].
A phase II randomized trial comparing enclomiphene with topical testosterone is published in Fertility and Sterility [3].
A BJU International report of a phase III trial in obese hypogonadal men is published [6].
A meta-analysis of randomized trials of clomiphene and enclomiphene in functional hypogonadism is published [4].
